title: Evaluation, Access & Operations
description: Study graph extraction metrics, retrieval and answer evaluation, authorization-aware traversal, and cost and graph maintenance. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Graph extraction metrics
lessons.description: Define relation-level correctness and review a stratified sample.
lessons.conceptOverview: Measure entity and relation precision and recall on labeled samples, including endpoint identity and qualifiers. A large edge count is not a quality metric and can increase noise.
lessons.whyItMatters: Graph growth must be evaluated for accuracy.

lessons.title: Retrieval and answer evaluation
lessons.description: Create a test with expected evidence and a supported-answer rubric.
lessons.conceptOverview: Evaluate evidence retrieval separately from answer faithfulness and completeness. Multi-hop tests should label required supporting edges and passages, not just compare final wording.
lessons.whyItMatters: Correct wording alone does not prove grounded reasoning.

lessons.title: Authorization-aware traversal
lessons.description: Design source-aware filtering and summary isolation.
lessons.conceptOverview: Apply access rules to nodes, edges and supporting sources before constructing context. Summaries derived from restricted sources can leak information even if the original documents are hidden.
lessons.whyItMatters: Derived graph summaries inherit relevant source restrictions.

lessons.title: Cost and graph maintenance
lessons.description: Compare graph and text-only retrieval on the same queries and operating budget.
lessons.conceptOverview: Extraction, resolution, summarization and indexing contribute to graph maintenance cost. Measure whether graph retrieval improves the target workload enough to justify these operations over a simpler baseline.
lessons.whyItMatters: GraphRAG should demonstrate value against a simpler baseline.
